prerequisites: See the individual tools. Almost everything downstream in the Sentinel tab depends on Project Setup having bound the model to a web project.
steps: Click the Standards drop-down arrow under Sentinel > Standards & Build.
Choose Project Setup, Sign in, Build Office System, Apply Standard or Ingest Docs.
tips: Project Setup and Sign in need no special permission; the build tools change the model and are normally used by the standards lead.

Sentinel_Setup.summary: Binds the open model to its web project and sets the project code, ghost source folder and Revit Doctor option.
overview: Project Setup is where a model is told which web project it belongs to, like picking an ACC or Forma project. The project's ruleset, IDS and naming standard all come from that web project (or its office), so most Sentinel tools refuse to do anything until this is saved.

Settings can be saved at two scopes. "Current project" stores them inside the Revit model (Extensible Storage), so they travel with the model and sync with central to the whole team. "This machine only" stores paths and defaults in %AppData%\Sentinel\config.json for this PC; at machine scope the web project, project code and Doctor option are switched off because they belong to a model.

Saving the web project at project scope also confirms, on this PC, that this model publishes into that project. Until a PC has confirmed the project for a model, Auto-publish and scan posts are paused on that PC (a copy or Save As of a model asks again). After saving, the ruleset for the chosen project is reloaded.
prerequisites: For project scope, a model must be open; with no model open only machine scope is available.

The Sentinel bridge should be running so the project list can load. If it is not, the Web project box is a plain text field and you type the project key (the hint says "Bridge unreachable - type the project key").
If you are signed out, the project list may not load ("Signed out - Sentinel > Sign in, or type the project key"). Typing the key still works.

inputs.name: Project code (optional - tightens the CDE file-name check, e.g. BDS20268)
inputs.desc: Your office's project code. It is saved in upper case and tightens the file-name check against the naming standard. Leave blank if you do not use one.

inputs.name: Web project - where this model publishes
inputs.desc: Pick a project from the list, or type its key (for example demo). The list shows each project's name and key, with its office. This is what binds the model.

inputs.name: Ghost source folder (DWGs, specs - drives Datum & Ghost Builder)
inputs.desc: A full local folder path where the source DWGs and specifications live; use Browse... to pick it. A share typed as a share path is refused for project scope; use a full path (a mapped drive is fine).

inputs.name: Revit Doctor checkbox
inputs.desc: When ticked, Revit straightens slightly off-axis lines in this model using its own fix in every transaction. Off by default; when off, the Doctor only logs the warnings it sees and never removes one. Bound models only.

inputs.name: Save scope
inputs.desc: "Current project (Extensible Storage - syncs with central, whole team)" or "This machine only (%AppData%\Sentinel\config.json - paths and defaults; never the web project)".

inputs.name: Save / Cancel
inputs.desc: Save writes the settings and closes; Cancel closes without saving.

steps: Open the model, then click Sentinel > Standards > Project Setup.
Choose the Web project from the list, or type its key.
Optionally enter the Project code and set the Ghost source folder with Browse....
Leave Save scope on "Current project" to bind the model, then click Save.

The dialog closes; the settings are written to the model and the project's ruleset reloads. If the model has never been saved to a file, save it and run Project Setup > Save again so this PC can confirm the project (the Doctor log says so).
results: At project scope: the web project key, project code, ghost folder and Doctor option are stored in the model as a Revit change named "Sentinel: Save project settings", and this PC records that it confirmed that project for this model.
At machine scope: the ghost source folder is written to %AppData%\Sentinel\config.json, and the dialog shows "Saved as machine default".
The Sentinel pane refreshes its ruleset and Next strip for the new project.
tips: A line under the Web project box says what Save confirms: that this model, on this PC, publishes into the named project.
The footer shows who the bridge will see: "Signed in as ..." or "Signed out"; use Sign in to change it.
A folder that cannot be used from a model (for example a share path rather than a full local path) shows a message and is not saved.
If the Web project hint says the bridge address is refused, the configured bridge address is not allowed and no token is sent to it; fix the Sentinel configuration.
Machine scope never binds a model; if tools say "not bound", save at project scope.

Sentinel_SignIn.summary: Signs you in with your Sentinel account so everything Revit sends to the project carries your name.
overview: Sign in uses the same e-mail and password as the Sentinel web app. Once signed in, every governed call from Revit (publishing, review, fixes, snapshots) is sent under your own session and the ledger records your e-mail. Signed out, Revit either uses this PC's shared machine token, in which case the ledger records the Windows user name rather than you, or, if no token is set, governed calls are refused.

The session is kept on this PC (encrypted for your Windows account) and survives restarting Revit. Sign out forgets it on this PC only; it does not sign you out of the web app. The password is used once to sign in and is not kept.
Some actions, such as installing a catalogue on the office, require you to be signed in as yourself because the bridge checks your role.
prerequisites: The PC's Sentinel configuration (%AppData%\Sentinel\bcf-config.json) must contain the Supabase address and key. Without them the dialog says sign-in is not possible on this PC and the Sign in button is disabled.
You need an existing Sentinel account; there is no sign-up here.
The bridge address in the configuration must be one Sentinel accepts; if it is refused the dialog shows the reason.

inputs.name: E-mail
inputs.desc: Your Sentinel account e-mail.

inputs.name: Password
inputs.desc: Your Sentinel account password. Press Enter or click Sign in.

inputs.name: Sign in / Sign out / Close
inputs.desc: Sign in is shown when signed out; Sign out replaces it when signed in. Close just closes the dialog.

steps: Click Sentinel > Standards > Sign in.
Type your E-mail and Password.
Click Sign in (or press Enter). The dialog shows "Signing in..." for up to about 8 seconds.
On success the top line reads "Signed in as <your e-mail> - the ledger records your e-mail." Click Close.
To forget the session on this PC, open the dialog again and click Sign out.
results: Your session is stored on this PC and used for every governed call from Revit; ledger rows show your e-mail.
Sign out removes the stored session on this PC only.
tips: Before signing in the top line reads either "Signed out - governed calls are refused until you sign in" or "Signed out - this PC's shared machine token is used, and the ledger records ... not you".
Failed sign-ins show Supabase's message (or "Supabase not reached") under the form.
If a stored session can no longer be refreshed, Sentinel signs you out and asks you to use Standards > Sign in again.
The dialog's footer shows which address it signs in at and which bridge it uses.

Sentinel_BuildOfficeSystem.summary: Reads the office standard out of the open "golden" model, lets you review and tick it, then builds it into this model and into the project's ruleset.
overview: Run this on the office's golden model or template. It reads, without changing anything, the user worksets, the shared-parameter bindings, the view templates, the Project Browser organisation schemes and the full catalogue of family and element types in that model. They appear in a review window, grouped, each with a confidence badge, and the items it is certain of are pre-ticked.

From the review window you can build the ticked items into the model, save them as a standards pack for other models, run an ISO 19650 gap check, send an office snapshot to the web project, or install the type catalogue on the office. Building also installs the ticked worksets and naming rules into the web project's ruleset so the scanner enforces them.

The type catalogue ("Families & Types") is reference only: nothing to tick or build. It is exported to a file at the start of the command, and a lead can install it on the office from the window so Ghost Builder, Photo Massing and Promote read the office's real types.
prerequisites: A Revit model open; it is the model the standard is read from, and the Build button writes into the model the window was opened on.
For the ruleset part of a build, the model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup); otherwise the model is built but the ruleset line says it was not installed because there is no project.
Workset items need a workshared model; on a model that is not workshared they are skipped with a message to enable worksharing.

View templates and browser organisation schemes are copied from the golden model, so it must be open in the same Revit session when you build into another model; otherwise they are skipped with a message to open the golden model.

Send office snapshot needs the model bound to a web project and a pack that came from a model. Install catalogue on office needs you signed in, a pack with a harvested catalogue, and a project that belongs to an office; the bridge checks that you are a lead on that office.
While the build runs, the model the window was opened on must still be open and active; if you switch to another model the build refuses and says nothing was changed.

inputs.name: Tree of items (checkboxes)
inputs.desc: Groups: Worksets, Shared Parameters, Naming Rules, View Templates, Browser Organization. Each row has a confidence badge (green high, amber medium, red low) and its provenance. Items from the golden model start ticked. Untick anything the office should not standardise.

inputs.name: Families & Types
inputs.desc: A read-only list of the types in the model by category, for reference. Nothing here is built.

inputs.name: Build ticked items
inputs.desc: Builds the ticked worksets, shared parameters, view templates and browser schemes into the model, and installs worksets and naming rules into the project's ruleset. If nothing is ticked it says so.

inputs.name: Save pack
inputs.desc: Saves the ticked items as a standards pack file, named after the source model and version, in %AppData%\Sentinel\packs.

inputs.name: ISO 19650 check
inputs.desc: Grades the whole proposed standard (not only the ticked part) against ISO 19650 fundamentals and shows the gaps.

inputs.name: Send office snapshot to Sentinel
inputs.desc: Sends this pack's worksets, shared parameters, type catalogue and current ruleset to the web project's Documents > READINESS view so the office standard can be measured.

inputs.name: Install catalogue on office
inputs.desc: Installs the harvested type catalogue as the office's type catalogue on the web app (a lead's action).

steps: Open the golden model or template and click Sentinel > Standards > Build Office System.
Wait for the extraction (it is read-only). The review window "Sentinel - Build Office System" opens, and a dialog reports that the type catalogue was exported and where.
Tick the items you want, and untick the rest.
Optionally click ISO 19650 to see the gaps, and Save pack to keep the pack for other models.
To build into a model, make that model the active document first, then click Build ticked items. (To build into a different, blank model, use Apply Standard there instead.)
Read the report in the window: created, skipped and failed items, followed by the "Ruleset install" outcome.
Optionally click Send office snapshot to Sentinel, or (as a lead, signed in) Install catalogue on office.
results: The window shows Created, Skipped and Failed lists, then the ruleset install result and a status line such as "Done - N created, N skipped, N failed".
The whole build is one Undo entry in Revit named "Apply standard"; if a step fails the build is rolled back.
Items that already exist are skipped, so rebuilding only adds what is missing.
Shared parameters are bound to the categories that exist in the model. They use the model's shared-parameter file if one is set; otherwise a file is created under %AppData%\Sentinel\shared.

When the model is bound and worksets or naming rules were ticked, the project's ruleset gains a new version containing them and the scanner reloads it. If the project was inheriting the office's ruleset, it now has its own and stops inheriting later office changes (the window warns).
If Revit kept the build and something was created, one "Apply Standard" row is written to the project ledger.
The type catalogue is exported to %AppData%\Sentinel\exports.
tips: The window title reads "Build Office System" for all three standards tools.

A cached copy of the ruleset is never used as the base for an install: if the bridge did not answer, the model is built but the ruleset is not installed, and the report says to run Apply again when the bridge is up.
Naming rules usually come from Ingest Docs; a golden model supplies worksets, parameters, view templates, browser schemes and the type catalogue.
Only one build can run at a time; pressing Build again while one is running says so.

Sentinel_LoadOfficeSystem.summary: Loads a saved standards pack from disk and lets you build it into the open model, the golden-to-blank round trip.
overview: Apply Standard opens a standards pack file (the kind Build Office System or the review window's Save pack writes), shows its contents in the same review window, and builds the ticked items into the model that is active when you start. Use it to bring the office worksets, shared parameters and rules into a new or blank model.

The build is the same as in Build Office System: items that already exist are skipped, the whole build is one Undo entry, and ticked worksets and naming rules are installed into the web project's ruleset when the model is bound.
prerequisites: A Revit model open (the target).
A standards pack file (.json), normally in %AppData%\Sentinel\packs.
For the ruleset install, the model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup); otherwise the model is still built and the report says no ruleset was installed.
Worksets need a workshared target model; otherwise they are skipped with a message.

View templates and browser schemes in the pack are copied from the pack's source model, which must be open in the same Revit session; otherwise they are skipped with a message naming the model to open.

inputs.name: Load Sentinel Standards Pack (file dialog)
inputs.desc: Choose a .json standards pack. The dialog opens in %AppData%\Sentinel\packs when that folder exists.

inputs.name: Review window tree and buttons
inputs.desc: Tick the items to build, then Build ticked items; the window also offers Save pack, ISO 19650 check, Send office snapshot to Sentinel and Install catalogue on office (see Build Office System).

steps: Open or create the target model and bind it to its web project (Project Setup) if you want the ruleset installed.
Click Sentinel > Standards > Apply Standard.
Pick the pack file in the "Load Sentinel Standards Pack" dialog.
In the review window, tick or untick items. The status line reads "N item(s) from '<file>'. Tick items, then Build into '<model>'."
Click Build ticked items and read the Created, Skipped and Failed report and the ruleset install result.
results: Worksets, shared-parameter bindings, view templates and browser schemes added to the active model as one Undo entry named "Apply standard".
Existing items are listed as skipped.
The project's ruleset gets a new version with the pack's worksets and naming rules when the model is bound and the bridge answers.
One "Apply Standard" row on the project ledger when Revit kept the build and something was created.
tips: "Could not read the standards pack" means the file is not valid pack JSON; the reason is shown.
"The selected file is not a valid standards pack" means the file was empty or not a pack.
The type catalogue shown in the window is reference only; nothing in it is built.
The Send office snapshot button needs a pack that came from a model; a pack with no source model says to extract from a template first.
If you switch to another model before pressing Build, the build refuses and changes nothing.

Sentinel_IngestDocs.summary: Reads office-standards documents with a local language model and proposes worksets, shared parameters and naming rules for you to review.
overview: Ingest Docs turns a written standard (a PDF, text, Markdown or CSV file) into a reviewable standards pack. You pick one or more documents; a local language model (Ollama, running on your PC) reads them in chunks and extracts workset names, required shared parameters (with data type, instance or type binding, and categories) and naming conventions for views, sheets, families, levels and grids.

The results open in the same review window as Build Office System, with the source file and page recorded for each item. Items found in documents are never pre-ticked: you decide what is real. Nothing is invented on purpose, but a language model can misread, so review each row.

From there you can build the ticked items into the open model, save them as a pack, or run the ISO 19650 check. Ticked worksets and naming rules also go into the web project's ruleset when you build. The documents are read on your own machine; by default nothing is sent to a cloud service.
prerequisites: Ollama running locally with a model pulled. The default is the model llama3 at http://localhost:11434; the PC can override the address and model with the SENTINEL_OLLAMA_URL and SENTINEL_LLM_MODEL settings. An address on another machine is refused unless this PC's configuration explicitly allows it.
A Revit model open (it is the model the pack would be built into).
Readable documents: .pdf, .txt, .md or .csv.
To build the results into a model: the same requirements as Build Office System (bound to a web project for the ruleset install; workshared for worksets).

inputs.name: Ingest office-standards documents (file dialog)
inputs.desc: Select one or more documents. Multiple files are allowed. The filter shows pdf, txt, md and csv; All files is also available.

inputs.name: Review window
inputs.desc: Tick items to keep, then Build ticked items or Save pack. A pack made from documents has no source model, so Send office snapshot and Install catalogue on office will say to extract from a template first.

steps: Start Ollama and make sure the model is available.
Click Sentinel > Standards > Ingest Docs.
Select the standards document(s) and click Open.
The review window opens at once with a status like "Reading N document(s) and querying the local LLM...". The first run loads the model and can take a minute or more; large documents take longer.
When extraction finishes the tree fills in. Tick only what is correct (nothing is pre-ticked).
Click Build ticked items to create the worksets and shared parameters in the model and add the worksets and naming rules to the ruleset, or Save pack to keep the pack for Apply Standard.
results: A review window with Worksets, Shared Parameters and Naming Rules extracted from the documents, each tagged with its file and page.
On build: the same Created, Skipped and Failed report, one Undo entry, ruleset install and ledger row as the other standards tools.
Saving writes a pack to %AppData%\Sentinel\packs, named after the first document.
Naming rules are given stable ids (NM-01, NM-02, ...) so re-running replaces rather than duplicates them.
tips: "The local LLM could not be reached ... Start Ollama and pull the model" means Ollama is not running or the model is not installed.
If one chunk of a document fails, the rest still produce results.
A message about the endpoint being refused means the configured model address is not local and this PC has not opted in to a remote one.
Document items carry a confidence below the golden-model level on purpose, which is why they start unticked.
"No worksets, shared parameters or naming rules were found in the document(s)" means the model found nothing it could extract; check the document actually contains readable text.

Sentinel_Roi.summary: Shows the web project's ledger counts for delivery gate runs, naming renames and family heals, and prices them if the project has an ROI standard.
overview: ROI Dashboard reads the open model's web project ledger and counts what Sentinel has done: delivery gate runs, naming renames and family heals. If the project (or its office) has an ROI standard installed (currency, hourly rate, minutes per action), each count is priced and a total is shown; without one it says money is not shown.

It also counts fixes that write ledger rows (auto-fixes, fix-in-place values written, Doctor resolutions) but does not price them, and it lists what it cannot count, such as CDE intercepts, MEP voids, BCF export and clash views, because those write no ledger row.
Every number is a count of ledger rows, so it reflects what happened on the web project, not just this model or session.
prerequisites: The model must be bound to a web project (Project Setup). Otherwise the window reads "ROI - not bound" and nothing is read.
The Sentinel bridge must be reachable. If it cannot be read the window says nothing was counted and gives the reason; a failed read is never shown as zero.
An ROI standard installed on the project or its office to see any money figures.
steps: Open the model bound to its web project.
Click Sentinel > Standards & Build > ROI Dashboard.
Revit pauses briefly while the ledger is read, then the "Return on investment" window opens.
Read the lines and close the window.
results: A window headed "Return on investment" whose first line states the project and how many ledger rows were read (and if only the newest were read because the ledger holds more).

Lines for: Delivery gate runs, Naming renames, Family heals (each with minutes and amount if priced), Money (total, currency and hourly rate, or why it is not shown), Fixes on the ledger (not priced), and Not counted.
Nothing is written to the model or the ledger.
tips: "Money: not shown - roi: ..." means no ROI standard is installed for the project or its office.
A count shown as "not priced - the roi sets no minutes for it" means the ROI standard has no minutes for that action.
If the ledger is large, only the newest rows are counted and the header says so.
The window is read-only and non-modal; you can keep it open while working.

Sentinel_Chain.summary: The Model from Drawings pulldown groups the seven tools that take a project from drawings or photos to a governed Revit model, in the order they are meant to be run.
overview: Model from Drawings is a pulldown, not a command of its own. Its seven entries are numbered in the order of the chain: 1 · Datum from Drawings, 2 · Ghost Builder, 2b · Photo Massing, 2c · Shell a Mass, 3 · Annotate Views, 4 · Promote (DD) and 5 · Provenance. The idea is datum first, then geometry, then views, then promotion to design-development (DD) types, with a stamp on everything Sentinel touches so you can always ask where an element came from.

Datum comes first because everything else hangs on it: real levels and a real grid, measured off your section and plan drawings, mean that walls built afterwards host to real floors and sit on a real column grid. Then you model geometry in one of two ways. Ghost Builder builds LOD 200 geometry from a 2D DWG plan. Photo Massing works from the project's evidence-pack photos instead: it estimates a building envelope (storeys, proportions) that you scale with one known dimension, and files a mass for review. Shell a Mass then turns a mass (yours, or the one Photo Massing made) into typed walls, floors and a roof, one storey at a time.

Annotate Views then creates the work-in-progress plan views, pins the datum and, if the guideline asks for it, makes sheets and tags. Promote (DD) retypes what is in the model to the office's exact DD types. Provenance reads back the stamp on any element.

How the tools are governed: Datum and Ghost Builder show you a review window and write only what you tick. Photo Massing, Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) do not write to the model themselves; they file their proposal as a changeset on the project's web ledger and open Review AI Proposals, where a person ticks and applies it. The standards that drive the chain (the layers standard, the office modelling guideline, the type catalogue, the LOD matrix) are installed on the project's web workspace or on the office. A standard that is not installed is shown as "none", and the tool says so instead of falling back on something else.
prerequisites: A Revit project open and active (Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) refuse to run in a family document).

For the changeset-based tools (Photo Massing, Shell a Mass, Promote (DD)) the model must be bound to a web project: use Project Setup first. Without it they stop with "This model is not bound to a web project".

The standards the chain reads must be installed on the project or its office: a layers standard (with a datum section) for Datum and Ghost Builder, a guideline for Ghost Builder, Shell a Mass, Annotate Views and Promote (DD), and a type catalogue for Shell a Mass and Promote (DD).
The Sentinel bridge must be running for the tools that file changesets or read the standards.
Ghost Builder and Photo Massing use a language or vision model that runs on your own PC (Ollama).
steps: Open the Sentinel tab and the Model from Drawings pulldown.
Run 1 · Datum from Drawings to create the levels and grids from your section and plan drawings.
Model the geometry: run 2 · Ghost Builder on a 2D DWG plan, or 2b · Photo Massing on the evidence-pack photos followed by 2c · Shell a Mass. You can use both, and model by hand in between.
Run 3 · Annotate Views to create the plan views (and sheets, if the guideline has them) and to pin the levels and grids.
Run 4 · Promote (DD) to retype walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, doors and windows to the office's DD types and open the result for review.
Use 5 · Provenance at any point to read where a single element came from.
results: Each tool reports in its own dialog. Datum and Ghost Builder write to the model after you press their own create or build button. Photo Massing, Shell a Mass and Promote (DD) put changesets into Review AI Proposals; nothing is placed until a person applies them.
Elements Sentinel places or changes carry a provenance stamp (source, source file, layer, rule, approver, ledger row, time).
tips: You do not have to run every step. The numbers are the recommended order, not a requirement; for example Annotate Views only needs levels in the model, wherever they came from.
Each tool that writes to the model does so as one Undo entry. Revit sometimes empties its Undo list afterwards; the tool's dialog and the ledger row then tell you what was made.
Sentinel never places into a design option. Switch to the Main Model first.

Sentinel_Datum.summary: Reads the levels from a section drawing and the grids from a plan drawing and creates them in the model, so that everything modelled afterwards sits on real heights and a real column grid.
overview: Datum from Drawings is the first step of the chain. It reads a DWG or DXF and finds the level lines and the grid lines on the layers that the project's layers standard names in its datum section. The heights and grid positions are measured straight off the drawing geometry; nothing is estimated and no language model is involved.

You see everything it found before anything is created. A review window lists every level and every grid with a tick box and a name, and for levels an elevation in millimetres from the zero level and a Building Story box. You untick lines that are not really levels or grids (a parapet line, a section mark), type your office's names, and say which level is zero. Only then does it create them.

A level at a height already in the model, or a grid on a line already in it, is kept and not duplicated, so you can run it again on another sheet. Each drawing has its own origin, so read the section for levels and the plan for grids as separate runs. When the run creates something, it also sends a datum row and a build receipt to the project's ledger.
prerequisites: A Revit project open. It must not be in a design option; if one is being edited the tool stops and asks you to switch to the Main Model.
Set the project base point and survey point first, as usual: the drawings are read origin to origin.
Drawings to read: either a Ghost source folder set in Project Setup that holds the project's DWG or DXF files, or a DWG already imported into the model. With neither, you get "No drawings to read".

A layers standard installed on the project or its office that has a datum section naming the layers for levels and grids. If the guideline cannot be read, the tool refuses rather than guess. If the standard has no datum section, the run finds nothing and lists the layers it saw so you can fix the standard or the drawing.
The Ghost source folder must be one this PC accepts; if it does not, the tool stops before reading anything.
If the guideline's placement block names a workset for Levels or Grids, the model must have that workset; otherwise the run is refused before anything is created.

inputs.name: Drawing list ("Sentinel — Datum: choose ONE drawing")
inputs.desc: Shown when a Ghost source folder is set. Pick the one drawing to read, then press "Use selected drawing ▶" (or double-click it). Use the section for levels and the plan for grids; run again for the other.

inputs.name: The drawing's units:
inputs.desc: "as the file says" by default. Choose millimetres, centimetres, metres, inches or feet if the drawing's own header is wrong.

inputs.name: Create (tick box)
inputs.desc: One per level and grid. Untick anything that is not a real level or grid.

inputs.name: Name
inputs.desc: The name the level or grid will get. Type your office's own labels.

inputs.name: ±0.00 at:
inputs.desc: Which level is the zero of the building. Levels below it read negative.

inputs.name: Elevation (mm from ±0.00)
inputs.desc: Editable height of each level.

inputs.name: Building Story
inputs.desc: Tick for levels that are storeys. Annotate Views and Promote rely on this.

inputs.name: Runs (mm)
inputs.desc: Shown for each grid so you can recognise it. Not editable.

steps: Open the project and click Model from Drawings, then "1 · Datum from Drawings".

If a Ghost source folder is set, choose a drawing in the list, set "The drawing's units:" if needed and press "Use selected drawing ▶". If no folder is set, the DWG already imported into the model is read directly.
Wait for the read. If nothing is found you get "Found no level or grid lines" with the layers the drawing holds.
In the review window untick lines that are not levels or grids, rename them, set "±0.00 at:" and the Building Story boxes.
Press "Create ▶". Cancel creates nothing.
Read the result dialog, rename in the Project Browser if needed, and continue with Ghost Builder or Annotate Views.
results: Levels and grids are created in the model, each stamped with where it came from.
A dialog reports how many levels and grids were created, what the placement block did, and any notes. It also suggests Annotate Views as the next step.
One datum row and one build receipt are sent to the project's ledger (the pane's log says what the ledger answered).
tips: Run once per drawing: sheets have different origins.
If "Nothing was created" appears, Revit did not commit; an element it needs may be owned by another user. The model is unchanged.
If the read finds nothing, check the datum section of the layers standard against the actual layer names in the drawing.
The unit setting matters: a drawing in metres read as millimetres gives levels at the wrong heights.

Sentinel_GhostBuilder.summary: Builds LOD 200 Revit geometry (walls, floors, doors, windows and more) from a 2D DWG plan, mapping CAD layers to Revit types by the project's standards, after you review and tick what to build.
overview: Ghost Builder takes a 2D plan drawing and proposes a model from it. It first imports the drawing for the run, reads the CAD layers and maps each layer to what it represents (walls, doors, windows, floors and so on). The mapping follows the project's layers standard first, then what it remembered for this project, then labelled heuristics, and only for what is left a language model that runs on your own PC. Nothing the model suggests is pre-ticked.

You then get a review window that lists the proposal by layer, with how many elements each layer holds, a type drop-down where the proposal is wrong, an option to ignore a layer, and a "Build on level:" box. Nothing has been built at that point. When you press "Build ticked layers ▶" the build is filed on the project's ledger as changesets from the drawing and placed in one step, with every element stamped with its source drawing and checksum. Walls are typed by the project's guideline and type catalogue; a type that is not installed is reported as a gap.

Revit stays usable while it works: the language model call and the reading of the standards run in the background, with a progress window you can cancel. Photos in the project's evidence pack, if any, and documents in the Ghost source folder are used as extra hints for the layer mapping only.
prerequisites: A Revit project open, in a plan view of the level you build on. Section, elevation, 3D and drafting views are refused because the imported drawing would lie in the wrong plane. Open a floor plan and run again.
A 2D DWG: either DWG or DXF files in the Ghost source folder (Project Setup), or a DWG import already in the model, which you pick on screen ("Select a 2D CAD (DWG) import to build from.").

The layers standard, guideline and type catalogue installed on the web project or its office, with the model bound via Project Setup. If the guideline cannot be read, the run stops. A standard that is not installed reads "none" in the review header. A model not bound to a project runs the build as a local changeset with no ledger.
The model should come from the office template: if it holds none of the office types in the installed catalogue, the run is refused and says so.

Ollama running on this PC with the Ghost model pulled. If it cannot be reached you are told to start Ollama and pull the model. Evidence photos are read by a vision model only if the model runs on this PC.
Not in a design option. If the mapping schema or family library folder named in this PC's config cannot be found, the tool tells you which one to fix or clear.

inputs.name: Choose a drawing ("Sentinel — Ghost Builder: choose a drawing")
inputs.desc: Shown when the Ghost source folder holds DWG/DXF files. Pick one and press "Use selected drawing ▶", or "Pick from model…" to use an import already in the model.

inputs.name: The drawing's units:
inputs.desc: "as the file says", millimetres, centimetres, metres, inches or feet. Set it if the file header is wrong.

inputs.name: Layer rows (tick boxes)
inputs.desc: One per mapped CAD layer. Tick the layers to build. Each row shows how it was mapped and a confidence score.

inputs.name: Type drop-down / (ignore)
inputs.desc: Change the type for a layer or set it to (ignore) where the proposal is wrong. Your picks are remembered for this project's next run.

inputs.name: Build on level:
inputs.desc: The level the elements are placed on. It opens on the level at the drawing's elevation, else the active plan's level, else the lowest.

steps: Open a floor plan of the level you build on.
Click Model from Drawings, then "2 · Ghost Builder".
If drawings are listed, select one, set "The drawing's units:" and press "Use selected drawing ▶". Otherwise select the CAD import in the view.
Wait while the standards are read, any photos and documents are used as hints, and the layers are mapped. Press Esc or Cancel in the progress window to stop.
In "Sentinel — Ghost Builder: review the build proposal", tick the layers to build, change types or choose (ignore) where the proposal is wrong, and check "Build on level:".
Press "Build ticked layers ▶".
If the build would add elements that your sync-blocking rules would stop, you are asked whether to place it anyway; going back keeps the review open and places nothing.
Read the summary dialog.
results: Elements are placed on the chosen level in one Undo entry, each stamped as from the source drawing. The imported DWG made for the run is removed again inside that Undo; an import you picked from the model is kept.

The summary names the standards used, how many elements were placed, how walls were typed (by the guideline, by the layer mapping, by you, or left as a gap), what was skipped and why, any types or families added, Revit warnings and the ledger line.
The build is also filed as changesets with source dwg on the project's ledger.
tips: Cancel, or closing the review without building, writes nothing and removes the imported drawing.

Doors and windows are only placed on a wall of the same build; the summary counts those skipped because no single straight wall was close enough, and those where the wall line stops short of the opening.
Run Datum from Drawings first so the build has real levels to host on.
Ghost Builder places directly after your Build click. Use Provenance on a built element to see the drawing and layer it came from.

Sentinel_Massing.summary: Estimates a building's storeys and proportions from the project's evidence-pack photos, lets you scale and correct the numbers, and files the missing levels and a mass for review.
overview: Photo Massing is for projects where you only have photos of the building. A vision model that runs on your own PC reads the admitted, blurred photos from the project's evidence pack and estimates storey count, height-to-width ratio, storey height, footprint and any openings it can see. These are an estimate: photos give counts and ratios, not lengths.

You supply one known dimension (the building's height or a facade's width, in metres) and press "Scale ▶"; the storey height and width are then worked out from it, while the depth is only assumed. You review every number in a window (amber fields are low confidence) and press "File for review ▶". That files one changeset on the project's ledger containing the Building Story levels the mass needs that the model lacks and one untyped mass between them.

Nothing is placed in the model by this tool. Review AI Proposals opens on the changeset and a person applies it there. After that, 2c · Shell a Mass turns the mass into typed walls, floors and a roof.
prerequisites: A Revit project open, bound to a web project (Project Setup), in a plan view. In any other view you are asked to open a plan view first.
Not in a design option.

Photos in the project's evidence pack that have been admitted and blurred (Files ▸ Evidence in the web app). With none, the tool says so and stops. Photos whose blurred copy cannot be fetched or does not match are skipped with a reason in the pane's log.
The Sentinel bridge running, so the evidence pack can be read and the changeset filed.
A vision model on this PC (Ollama). Photos are never sent to a model off this PC; the tool refuses before reading anything.
No review window open and no other filing in progress; otherwise the tool tells you to finish or wait.

inputs.name: Where does the mass stand?
inputs.desc: First choice. "Pick its footprint" uses a closed CAD polyline, a property line or model lines you selected first. "Width × depth from the photos" centres a box on a point you click.

inputs.name: Known height (m) / Known width (m)
inputs.desc: Type exactly one known dimension. With a picked footprint only the height row is offered.

inputs.name: Scale ▶
inputs.desc: Works out the storey height and width from the known dimension.

inputs.name: Storeys, Height : width, Storey height (mm), Footprint width/depth (mm)
inputs.desc: The estimate. Correct any value that is wrong; amber fields need your attention.

inputs.name: Rotation (°)
inputs.desc: Turns the footprint counter-clockwise about its centre; 0 leaves it.

inputs.name: Opening rows
inputs.desc: Windows and doors the model saw, with width and height. They are counted but not placed.

steps: Open a plan view of the model and click Model from Drawings, then "2b · Photo Massing".
In "Where does the mass stand?" choose the footprint option or the width-and-depth option. For the footprint option pick the outline; then pick a point for the centre if asked.
Wait while the photos are read ("Reading photo i of n" in the progress window).
In "Sentinel — Massing: review the estimate before filing" type one known dimension and press "Scale ▶".
Check and correct the numbers and compare the storey count with the photos.
Press "File for review ▶".
results: One changeset with the missing Building Story levels and a mass is filed on the project's ledger. Review AI Proposals opens on it by itself; a person ticks and applies it.
A receipt for the vision run is sent to the ledger. If a Photo Massing changeset is already waiting, that one opens instead of a second being filed.
If filing fails, a dialog says nothing was placed and nothing in the model changed.
tips: If no photo gives a reading, you get "Nothing was read" with each photo's reason.
A picked footprint must be one closed outline with at least three corners; otherwise the tool says why it cannot be used.
An older Photo Massing changeset that was read outside the evidence pack must be declined in Review AI Proposals before you run it again.
A model's storey count can be wrong in the same way on every photo; check it against the photos.

Sentinel_ShellMass.summary: Turns a selected mass into typed walls, a floor per level and a flat roof, one storey at a time, filed for review as changesets.
overview: Shell a Mass takes a mass in the model and cuts it at each Building Story level. For every storey it plans walls from that level to the next, with the exterior face on the mass face, a floor for the level and a flat roof on top. The types come from the office modelling guideline and the type catalogue installed on the project or its office. A curtain wall is used where a facade rule in the guideline says so, with the facade judged against True North.

It first shows you the plan in a dialog. Yes files it; No is a read-only run that changes nothing. Nothing is pre-ticked in the review that follows, and nothing is placed until a person applies it in Review AI Proposals.
A storey that leans or is not a single loop with straight edges is not planned; it is sent to a person with the reason shown in the dialog.
prerequisites: A Revit project open (not a family), bound to a web project through Project Setup.

A mass in the model: an in-place mass, a mass family, a mass made as a direct shape, or the mass from Photo Massing once its changeset has been applied. Select it first or pick it when asked. With no mass at all you are told to model one, place a mass family or run Photo Massing. If no mass shows in the current view you are told to turn on Show Mass or select the mass first.
Building Story levels in the model that the mass crosses (Datum from Drawings can create them).
A guideline and a type catalogue installed on the project or its office. With no guideline, or no catalogue, the tool says so and plans nothing.
The Sentinel bridge running.
No other review window or filing in progress.

inputs.name: The mass
inputs.desc: Select one mass before clicking, or pick it when prompted ("Pick the mass to shell").

inputs.name: Yes / No in the plan dialog
inputs.desc: Yes files the shell for review. No is a read-only run.

steps: Select the mass (or leave nothing selected and pick it when asked).
Click Model from Drawings, then "2c · Shell a Mass".
Wait while the bridge is read in the background. Revit stays usable and the dialog opens by itself.
Read the dialog: it names the standards used, lists the plan, says how many elements go into how many changesets, and lists the rows sent to a person (expand for details).
Press Yes to file, or No to stop with nothing filed.
Review AI Proposals opens on the first changeset. Tick the elements you want and apply.
results: One changeset up to 200 elements (one review, one Undo), or one changeset per storey above that. The first opens for review; the rest are listed in Review AI Proposals.
A receipt for the planning is sent to the ledger.
Rows sent to a person ride on the first changeset filed.
tips: If a Promote or Shell changeset is still waiting for review, it opens instead; apply or decline it, then run Shell a Mass again.
Once one storey is applied, walls stand inside the mass and Shell a Mass will not plan the rest of it. If only some storey changesets were filed, decline them and run it again.
If the mass cannot be shelled, the dialog says why and nothing is planned or filed.
Show Mass in the Massing & Site tab makes in-place masses visible so you can pick them.

Sentinel_Annotate.summary: Creates the work-in-progress plan views the guideline prescribes for each level, pins levels and grids, and optionally copies view templates and makes sheets with tags.
overview: Annotate Views is the third step of the chain. It reads the views section of the office modelling guideline installed on the project or its office and plans the floor plan and ceiling plan views for each level. Each view name comes from the project's view-naming rule, or a fixed WIP name, and is checked against Scan Now's naming rule before anything is created.

A preview window shows everything first. Story levels get the guideline's first floor plan and first ceiling plan entry pre-ticked; other views are listed unticked; a row that cannot be made is greyed with its reason. The same window lists every unpinned level and grid (story levels and grids are pre-ticked) so you can pin them in the same run.

If the guideline has a sheets block, you can also choose one level for which to make sheets and tags: sheets on the guideline's title block with the view placed on them, and tags for categories such as rooms. Those rows are never pre-ticked. If the guideline names view templates the model lacks, you are offered to copy them from an office template file you pick; the file is opened in the background and is never saved or changed.
prerequisites: A Revit project open with levels in it; with none you are told to run Datum from Drawings first.
The project's ruleset must be loaded: run Scan Now once, otherwise the tool refuses because it cannot judge the view names.
A guideline with a views section installed on the project or its office. Without it, there is nothing to plan and the tool says so.
At least one level should be a Building Story; otherwise no view or level is pre-ticked (unpinned grids still are).

For sheets: a sheets block in the guideline and its title block family loaded in the model. For tags: the tag families loaded. Sentinel loads no families; a row that needs a missing family is refused with the family name.
The model needs default floor plan and ceiling plan view types.

inputs.name: View rows (tick boxes)
inputs.desc: Grouped by level. Each shows name, use and template. Tick the views to create.

inputs.name: Pin rows
inputs.desc: Unpinned levels and grids to pin. A level or grid that another user owns, or that changed in central, is listed unticked with the reason.

inputs.name: Sheets and tags for:
inputs.desc: Choose one level to plan sheets and tags for, or leave it unset. Tick a sheet row to enable its tag rows.

inputs.name: Pick the office template file…
inputs.desc: Offered when view templates named by the guideline are missing. Choose an .rte or .rvt file, or "Continue without them".

steps: Click Model from Drawings, then "3 · Annotate Views".
If asked about missing view templates, pick the office template file or continue without them.
In "Sentinel — Annotate: views and pins" read the lines at the top, then tick or untick views and pins. Optionally choose a level in "Sheets and tags for:" and tick sheets and tags.
Press "Create ▶". Cancel writes nothing.
Read the result dialog.
results: Views, pins, copied view templates, sheets with viewports and tags are created in one Undo entry named Annotate views. Each view is made on its own: one that fails is rolled back and named, and the rest are kept.
The dialog lists what was created and pinned, what was not created and why, failures and warnings.
One annotate row goes to the ledger naming the views and datums the model holds.
tips: Revit may empty its Undo list after views are named. If Edit ▸ Undo does not list Annotate views, the ledger row is the record of which views to delete and which datums to unpin by hand.
Views already in the model are skipped, not duplicated.
If every ticked row fails, the dialog says nothing was created and the model is as it was.
Scan Now judges the new view names by the same rule, so names that pass here pass there.

Sentinel_PromoteWalls.summary: Promotes the model's walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, doors and windows to design-development types by the office guideline, type catalogue and LOD matrix, filing the changes for review.
overview: Promote (DD) looks at what is in the model and plans how to bring it to the office's DD standard. It retypes walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, doors and windows to the exact catalogue type already loaded in the model, swaps doors and windows to an office family type keeping their host, attaches wall tops to story levels, and re-creates wall-like and floor-like direct shapes as office types. Structural columns and beams are retyped by section when the catalogue has rows for them; these are never pre-ticked and sit outside the LOD matrix.

Anything ambiguous is not guessed: it is sent to a person with its reason. A dialog shows the plan per storey and per element class, the DD state now, the type gaps (elements for which the office has no type), and the foreign types found. Yes files the plan; No is a read-only run.

Filing creates one changeset per storey on the project's ledger, and Review AI Proposals opens on the first. Nothing is written to the model until a person ticks the elements and applies the changeset. No type is ever created, each change is stamped, and an Undo of it is recorded on the ledger.
prerequisites: A Revit project open (not a family), bound to a web project through Project Setup.
The Sentinel bridge running; otherwise you get "Couldn't reach the bridge".
An office modelling guideline (the DD rule file) installed on the project or its office. Without it, nothing is planned.
A type catalogue installed, and a model made from the office template: if the model holds none of the office types, the tool refuses and says so. Foreign types are still classified and reported.
An LOD matrix installed to cover floors, roofs, ceilings, doors and windows. With no matrix, Promote handles walls only.
To rehost a door or window you must be signed in; a rehost is only proposed when signed in.
No review window open and no other filing in progress.

inputs.name: Yes / No in the plan dialog
inputs.desc: Yes files one changeset per storey. No is a read-only run: nothing is filed, but the LOD state and type-gap rows are still sent to the ledger.

inputs.name: Sent to a person (expanded section)
inputs.desc: Expand it to read, per storey and element, why Sentinel would not decide.

steps: Make sure nothing from a previous Promote or Shell run is still waiting in Review AI Proposals.
Click Model from Drawings, then "4 · Promote (DD)". Revit stays usable while the bridge is read.
Read the dialog: the standards used, the plan lines per storey and class, the DD now counts, the LOD state, type gaps and foreign types.
Press Yes to file, or No to leave without filing. A storey whose every change was declined in an earlier review is not filed again.
Review AI Proposals opens on the first storey. Tick the changes and apply.
results: Changesets, one per storey, on the project's ledger and opened for review. Applying retypes or swaps elements in the model, each stamped by Promote.
Ledger rows for the LOD state now, the type gaps, the foreign types and a run receipt.
A type edit whose source the bridge cannot confirm is not filed with the retypes; it is listed as sent to a person.
tips: If a previous Promote or Shell changeset is still waiting, it opens instead of a new plan. Apply or decline it, then run Promote again.
Revit is asked first whether each retype is valid; a refused one is held with the reason, so one bad swap does not roll back a storey.
Elements already on other office types are left as is and counted apart.
If the model is re-bound to another project during the run, nothing is filed; run Promote again.
Use Provenance on a promoted element to see its stamp.

Sentinel_Provenance.summary: Shows where the selected element came from: Sentinel's provenance stamp in plain words.
overview: Provenance reads the stamp that Sentinel puts on elements it places or changes (Datum from Drawings, Ghost Builder, Shell a Mass, Promote and others) and describes it in a dialog. It only reads; nothing in the model changes and nothing goes over the network.

The dialog names the element (category, id and name) and then says whether Sentinel placed or changed it, the source, the checksum (sha256) of the source file, the CAD layer, the rule that typed it, the approver, the ledger row of the proposal and the time. A stamp that came along with a copy reads "Copied, not placed by Sentinel" and shows that the lines below belong to the original element.
prerequisites: A Revit project open.
An element to read: select exactly one element before clicking, or pick one when asked.

inputs.name: Element
inputs.desc: Select one element first. With no selection or several elements selected you pick one at the prompt "Pick an element to read its Sentinel provenance stamp".

steps: Select one element in the model.
Click Model from Drawings, then "5 · Provenance". If you did not select exactly one element, pick one when prompted; Esc cancels.
Read the dialog.
results: A dialog "Sentinel — Provenance" with the stamp. If there is no stamp it says Sentinel did not place or change this element.
tips: Fields a stamp did not record are said so, for example no source file for an element that came from a drawing already imported in the model, or an approver shown as unsigned (sign in so your name is recorded).
Older stamps read "not recorded" for the newer fields.
Copying an element copies its stamp, so check the first line of the dialog.
